project.name: Dashboard UX Sprint A — Visual System & Core Cockpits

summary: Comprehensive UI/UX uplift of the SpendCube React dashboard to maximise speed-to-insight for category managers. Sprint A covers: a semantic colour/typography foundation, enriched KPI cards with delta indicators, a treemap-based Overview page with spend signals, a fragmentation-first Category cockpit, a side-drawer Supplier profile, an opportunity-ranked Payment Terms page, a collapsible context-aware FilterBar, and chart interaction affordances (click hints, empty states, % labels). All changes are purely frontend — no backend or Python pipeline modifications.

decisions.recharts_treemap: Use Recharts Treemap component (already a dependency) for category spend composition. More readable than pie for 6-10 categories at different scales.
decisions.shadcn_sheet_for_supplier: Use shadcn/ui Sheet (side drawer) for supplier detail panel. Keeps the supplier table visible while showing detail — avoids the current below-table append that requires scrolling.
decisions.semantic_color_tokens: Add semantic CSS custom properties (--color-opportunity, --color-risk, --color-attention) in index.css. Extend tailwind config with these as named colors so utility classes like bg-opportunity/10 work.
decisions.collapsible_filterbar: FilterBar collapses to a single pill row by default. Expand button opens the full filter panel. Active filters displayed as removable pills even when collapsed.
decisions.no_backend_changes: All enhancements are frontend-only. Supplier detail charts will use supplier_id query param on existing cube endpoints; fall back to client-side filtering if the backend does not support that param.
decisions.treemap_library: Recharts Treemap is available from the existing recharts import. No new dependencies needed.
decisions.section_header_pattern: A reusable .section-header utility class (border-l-2 border-primary pl-2 text-sm font-semibold mb-3) added via @layer utilities in index.css.

existing_tables.transactions: Main fact table — all spend rows with canonical fields

userStories.title: SpendTreemap chart component
userStories.description: Create a SpendTreemap chart component using Recharts Treemap. Accepts data as [{name, value, color?}], renders with name and formatted value labels inside each cell, calls onCellClick(name) when a cell is clicked. Shows an empty state when data is empty.
acceptanceCriteria: Create file: frontend/src/components/charts/SpendTreemap.tsx
Export default function SpendTreemap with props: data: { name: string; value: number; color?: string }[], title: string, valueFormatter?: (v: number) => string, onCellClick?: (name: string) => void
Render a title h3 with className='section-header' above the treemap
Use Recharts Treemap: import { Treemap, ResponsiveContainer } from 'recharts'. Wrap in ResponsiveContainer width='100%' height={320}

Pass data to Treemap as the data prop with dataKey='value'. Use a custom content prop to render each cell: a React component that receives x, y, width, height, name, value. Render a rect with fill from the item color or CHART_COLORS[index % CHART_COLORS.length]. Inside the cell, if width > 60 and height > 40 render a text element for name (truncated to 16 chars) and a second text element for the formatted value — both white, font-size 11, centered in the cell.
When onCellClick is provided, the Treemap onClick handler calls onCellClick(payload.name)

If data is empty or every value is 0, render:
No data available
instead of the chart
Edit file: frontend/src/components/charts/index.ts — add: export { default as SpendTreemap } from './SpendTreemap'
Run: cd frontend && npm run build — should succeed with zero TypeScript errors

Group 2: label 'WACC %' text-xs, Input type='number' min=1 max=20 step={0.5} value={waccPct} onChange={e => setWaccPct(Number(e.target.value))} className='w-20'. userStories.title: Collapsible FilterBar with active filter pills

Include pills for: date_from (if set: label='From: '+date_from, onRemove clears it), date_to (same), each entry in business_units (label=value, onRemove removes it), each entry in category_l1s, supplier_search (if non-empty: label='Supplier: '+supplier_search), each legal_entity, each currency, each country, each abc_segment entry. When !expanded render: a single flex-row div className='flex items-center gap-2 flex-wrap py-2': (1) Button variant='outline' size='sm' onClick={() => setExpanded(true)}: Filters {activePills.length > 0 && {activePills.length}}. (2) For each activePill: a span className='inline-flex items-center gap-1 bg-muted text-muted-foreground text-xs rounded-full px-2.5 py-1': pill.label + an X button (button onClick={pill.onRemove}). (3) If activePills.length > 0: a button className='text-xs text-muted-foreground underline ml-1' onClick={() => onChange(defaultFilters())} text 'Clear all'.

When expanded render: the existing full filter UI (all current JSX) wrapped in the existing container div. At the end of the filter controls row, add a Button variant='ghost' size='sm' onClick={() => setExpanded(false)} text 'Close ↑'.
The component starts collapsed (expanded=false) by default — this is intentional so pages start clean.
Run: cd frontend && npm run build — should succeed with zero TypeScript errors
